newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Motta sees Senate OK of Brazil telecom law by Aug.
newsitem.headline: Motta sees Senate OK of Brazil telecom law by Aug.

text.p: Brazilian Communications Minister Sergio Motta on Thursday said he expects a new telecommunications law to be approved by the Senate by August.
"I believe the General Telecommunications Law will be approved in the Senate by August," Motta told reporters.
Motta praised Wednesday's lower house approval of the law which regulates and creates a watchdog for the sector and authorizes the privatization of the federal Telebras system.
The bill was entirely approved by the Chamber of Deputies, which completed voting on amendments to the law Thursday.

Speaking at an international meeting of ministers on postal services, Motta confirmed the government's plans to invest $91 billion in the telecommunications sector between 1995 and 2003. Previously, the government's investment plan amounted to $75 billion.
Motta also said Brazil plans to invest $40 billion by 1999, of which $2 billion will go to the federally owned postal service.
The Communications Minister said the Brazilian government aims to create a new law to regulate and open the country's postal services to private capital.
